summary: Computing is broken into sixteen capabilities that follow the layers of a software system: languages and development tooling, testing, requirements and design (SWEBOK v4 knowledge areas and ACM CCS 'Software and its engineering'); embedded toolchains; application frameworks; databases by DB-Engines data model and data integration (ACM CCS 'Information systems'); operating systems, cloud infrastructure and networks (CNCF landscape and ACM CCS 'Networks'); security split along NIST CSF 2.0 functions; storage; IT operations by ITIL 4 practice; and machine-learning platforms. O*NET's UNSPSC categories decided where products sit, and mainstream tools (Python, C, C++, Java, SQL, Git, Linux, Kubernetes) lead their nodes.

capabilities.name: Programming languages and compilers
capabilities.definition: Given source code in a programming language, translate it into executable form and run it with the semantics the language defines.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > General programming languages
Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers
Object or component oriented development software

onet_categories: Object or component oriented development software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'General-purpose programming languages, compilers and runtimes'. Split by execution model (ahead-of-time native, managed bytecode, dynamic interpreter, parallel and accelerator) because each has its own benchmark suites. Shell languages moved to operating systems; R, MATLAB and SAS stay with science as numerical and statistical tools; hardware description languages go to design.

tasks.name: Ahead-of-time native compilation
tasks.definition: Given source in a compiled systems language, produce optimized machine code for a target processor that preserves program semantics.
tasks.inputs: source code, target architecture, optimization settings

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers

onet_products: American National Standards Institute ANSI C
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SPEC CPU and LLVM test-suite measure generated-code speed; Csmith-style random programs test correctness

tasks.name: Managed bytecode runtimes
tasks.definition: Given programs compiled to a portable bytecode, execute them with just-in-time compilation, garbage collection and runtime type safety.
tasks.inputs: bytecode or intermediate language, runtime configuration
tasks.outputs: running program, throughput and pause-time profile

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers > Just-in-time compilers

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: DaCapo, Renaissance and SPECjbb measure JIT and garbage-collector performance
tasks.notes: ABAP and Solidity are languages bound to one platform (SAP, Ethereum virtual machine); listed here because the function is still compiling and running a language.

tasks.name: Dynamic language interpreters
tasks.definition: Given source in a dynamically typed scripting language, parse and execute it interactively or as a program.
tasks.inputs: script source, libraries, interpreter options

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers > Interpreters

onet_products: Microsoft Visual Basic for Applications VBA
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: pyperformance, JetStream and similar suites measure interpreter speed; conformance suites such as test262 check semantics
tasks.notes: TypeScript and Julia compile, but are used and benchmarked as dynamic scripting languages.

tasks.name: Parallel and accelerator programming
tasks.definition: Given a computation, express it for multicore, distributed-memory or GPU execution and generate efficient parallel code.
tasks.inputs: sequential or annotated source, target hardware
tasks.outputs: parallel kernels or programs, scaling and throughput figures

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > General programming languages > Language types > Parallel programming languages

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAS Parallel Benchmarks and KernelBench give reference kernels with correctness checks and speed targets

tasks.name: Interface definition and code generation
tasks.definition: Given an interface or schema definition, generate client, server and serialization code in one or more languages.
tasks.inputs: interface definition (IDL, protocol schema, WSDL)
tasks.outputs: generated stubs, serializers and type definitions

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers > Source code generation

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: conformance suites (for example the Protocol Buffers conformance tests) check generated code, but quality beyond correctness is hard to score

tasks.name: Source-to-source translation and migration
tasks.definition: Given a program in one language or platform version, produce an equivalent program in another.
tasks.inputs: legacy source code, target language or platform
state_of_art: IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: parallel corpora with unit tests (CodeXGLUE code-to-code, TransCoder test sets) score functional equivalence

capabilities.name: Software development tooling
capabilities.definition: Given a codebase and a change to make, provide the editing, generation, versioning, review, build and delivery machinery that turns the change into a released artifact.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Development frameworks and environments
App Definition and Development > Continuous Integration & Delivery

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Development environments, build, version control and collaboration'. Kept as one capability with eight tasks; AI code generation added as its own task because it now has the strongest public benchmarks in the domain. Infrastructure configuration tools (Puppet, Chef, Ansible) went to cloud infrastructure, not here, even though O*NET files them under configuration management.

tasks.name: Code editing and refactoring
tasks.definition: Given a codebase, let a developer navigate, edit and apply semantics-preserving refactorings with language-aware assistance.
tasks.inputs: source tree, language server or index

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Development frameworks and environments > Integrated and visual development environments

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: automated refactorings can be checked for behavior preservation with tests, but editor productivity is not directly scorable

tasks.name: Code generation from natural language
tasks.definition: Given a natural-language task and a codebase or function signature, produce a code change that makes the specified tests pass.
tasks.inputs: task description, repository or signature, tests

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Compilers > Source code generation

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench score generated code against hidden tests
tasks.notes: No O*NET product names a coding assistant directly; ChatGPT is listed under development environment software.

tasks.name: Version control and merging
tasks.definition: Given a sequence of edits by many authors, record history, branch, and merge concurrent changes with conflict detection.
tasks.inputs: working tree changes, branches
tasks.outputs: commit history, merged trees, conflict reports

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Software post-development issues > Software version control

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: historical merge commits give ground-truth resolutions to score automatic merge-conflict resolution

tasks.name: Code hosting and review
tasks.definition: Given proposed changes to a shared repository, host them, run review discussion and gate merges on approvals and checks.
tasks.inputs: repositories, pull or merge requests
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: datasets of real review comments (for example Microsoft CodeReviewer) score automated review, but review value is partly subjective

tasks.name: Build automation and dependency management
tasks.definition: Given source, build scripts and declared dependencies, resolve versions, fetch packages and produce build artifacts incrementally and reproducibly.
tasks.inputs: source, build files, dependency manifests, package repositories
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: build time, incremental rebuild cost and bit-for-bit reproducibility are measurable, but no shared suite exists

tasks.name: Continuous integration and delivery
tasks.definition: Given commits to a repository, automatically build, test and promote them through environments to release.
tasks.inputs: repository events, pipeline definitions, environments
tasks.outputs: build and test results, deployed releases
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: pipeline latency and flaky-test handling can be measured on fixed repositories, but no standard suite exists

tasks.name: Issue and defect tracking
tasks.definition: Given bug reports and work items, record, deduplicate, triage and track them to resolution.
tasks.inputs: reports, work items, triage rules
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: public bug trackers give ground truth for duplicate detection and triage assignment; the workflow itself is not scorable
tasks.notes: Jira is also a general project tool; see enterprise for project management.

tasks.name: API documentation generation
tasks.definition: Given annotated source code, extract and render reference documentation for its interfaces.
tasks.inputs: source with doc comments

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Software post-development issues > Documentation

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: code-summarization datasets (CodeSearchNet) score generated descriptions, extraction itself is deterministic

capabilities.name: Software testing and verification
capabilities.definition: Given a program and its specification or tests, find defects, show the absence of classes of defects, or locate their cause.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Software verification and validation

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Software testing, debugging and verification'. Tasks follow SWEBOK test levels and techniques plus static, formal and dynamic analysis. Usability testing (Morae, UserZoom) handed to media as interaction design research.

tasks.name: Unit test authoring and execution
tasks.definition: Given a unit of code, write and run tests that check its behavior and measure coverage and fault detection.
tasks.inputs: source code, specification or existing tests
tasks.outputs: test cases, pass/fail results, coverage and mutation scores

crosswalk.label: Software Testing > Test levels > Unit testing

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Defects4J and TestGenEval score generated tests by coverage and by real faults detected

tasks.name: User interface test automation
tasks.definition: Given a web, desktop or mobile application, drive its user interface through scripted scenarios and check expected states.
tasks.inputs: application under test, test scripts or scenarios
onet_products: Hewlett-Packard HP TestDirector for Quality Center
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: suites of instrumented apps with seeded faults can score fault detection, but scenarios are application-specific

tasks.name: Service interface testing
tasks.definition: Given an API specification and a running service, generate and send requests and check responses against the specification.
tasks.inputs: API specification (OpenAPI, WSDL), service endpoint
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: open REST services with known faults (the EvoMaster benchmark corpus) score coverage and faults found

tasks.name: Load and performance testing
tasks.definition: Given a system and a workload model, generate concurrent load and measure throughput, latency and failure points.
tasks.inputs: workload profile, target system
onet_products: Network and application load and performance testing software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: generator accuracy can be checked against a reference service, but the target system is the variable

tasks.name: Static code analysis
tasks.definition: Given source code, find defects and rule violations without executing it.
tasks.inputs: source code, rule set
tasks.outputs: findings with locations, severities and traces

crosswalk.label: Software Quality > Software quality management techniques > Static techniques

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the NIST Juliet test suite and OWASP Benchmark have labeled true and false positives

tasks.name: Formal software verification
tasks.definition: Given a program and a formal specification, prove that the program meets it or produce a counterexample.
tasks.inputs: program, specification or assertions

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Software verification and validation > Formal software verification

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SV-COMP publishes verification tasks with known verdicts

tasks.name: Debugging and fault localization
tasks.definition: Given a failing program and a failure, locate the faulty code and, where possible, propose a repair.
tasks.inputs: program, failing input or test, execution
tasks.outputs: suspicious locations, root cause, candidate patch

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Software verification and validation > Software defect analysis > Software testing and debugging

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Defects4J and BugsInPy give real bugs with developer fixes to score localization and repair

tasks.name: Performance and memory profiling
tasks.definition: Given a running program, attribute time, memory and resource use to code locations and detect leaks.
tasks.inputs: instrumented or sampled execution
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: programs with planted hot spots and leaks can score attribution accuracy, but no standard suite exists

capabilities.name: Requirements and software architecture
capabilities.definition: Given stakeholder needs, produce traceable requirements, design models and architecture descriptions, and estimate the effort to build them.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software creation and management > Designing software > Requirements analysis
Requirements analysis and system architecture software

onet_categories: Requirements analysis and system architecture software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Requirements, modeling and architecture'. Added software effort estimation (SWEBOK engineering economics) because O*NET lists QSM SLIM and it has public datasets. Capacity planning moved to IT operations, where ITIL places it.

tasks.name: Requirements capture and traceability
tasks.definition: Given stakeholder statements and design artifacts, record requirements, classify them and maintain trace links to design and tests.
tasks.inputs: stakeholder statements, documents, existing artifacts
tasks.outputs: requirement set, trace matrix, change impact
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: the PROMISE NFR dataset and trace-link recovery datasets score classification and tracing

tasks.name: Software design modeling
tasks.definition: Given requirements, build structural and behavioral models (classes, components, states, sequences) and generate or check code against them.
tasks.inputs: requirements, domain concepts
tasks.outputs: UML or similar models, generated code skeletons
onet_products: Computer aided software engineering CASE tools
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: model-to-code consistency can be checked, but design quality is judged, not computed

tasks.name: Architecture description and analysis
tasks.definition: Given a system's components and connectors, describe its architecture and analyze qualities such as dependency structure and performance.
tasks.inputs: component and connector descriptions, quality scenarios
tasks.benchmarkable: no: architecture quality has no agreed ground truth beyond specific metrics

tasks.name: Software effort estimation
tasks.definition: Given the size and characteristics of a planned software project, estimate effort, duration and staffing.
tasks.inputs: size measures (function points, lines of code), project factors
tasks.outputs: effort and schedule estimates with uncertainty
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: PROMISE and ISBSG project datasets with actual effort allow error scoring

capabilities.name: Embedded and real-time toolchains
capabilities.definition: Given firmware for a microcontroller, signal processor or real-time computer, compile, configure, load, debug and verify it on the target hardware.

crosswalk.label: Computer systems organization > Embedded and cyber-physical systems > Embedded systems > Embedded software
Computer systems organization > Real-time systems > Real-time operating systems

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Embedded and real-time toolchains'. Places existing function 'firmware' whole. Model-based code generation sits here; designing the control law sits in simulate. PLC and ladder logic belong to produce.

tasks.name: Cross-compilation for embedded targets
tasks.definition: Given firmware source and a microcontroller or DSP target, produce a size- and speed-optimized image that fits the target's memory map.
tasks.inputs: C, C++ or assembly source, linker script, target device
tasks.outputs: firmware image, memory map, size report

crosswalk.label: Computer systems organization > Embedded and cyber-physical systems > Embedded systems > Embedded software

onet_products: Texas Instruments Code Composer Studio CCStudio
Wind River Systems C/C++ Compiler Suite
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Embench and EEMBC CoreMark measure code size and speed on fixed reference programs

tasks.name: Real-time operating system configuration
tasks.definition: Given tasks with priorities and deadlines, configure and run a real-time kernel that schedules them deterministically.
tasks.inputs: task set, timing requirements, board support package
tasks.outputs: configured kernel image, scheduling and latency behavior

crosswalk.label: Computer systems organization > Real-time systems > Real-time operating systems

onet_products: Real time operating system RTOS software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Thread-Metric and interrupt-latency tests give comparable kernel timings on a fixed board

tasks.name: On-target debugging and trace
tasks.definition: Given a running embedded target, halt, step, inspect memory and registers, and capture execution trace through a debug probe.
tasks.inputs: target board, debug probe, symbol files
tasks.outputs: breakpoints, register and memory views, trace logs
tasks.benchmarkable: no: tool quality depends on hardware support and workflow, not a scorable output

tasks.name: Model-based embedded code generation
tasks.definition: Given a block diagram or state-machine model of controller behavior, generate production embedded code equivalent to the model.
tasks.inputs: controller model, target and data-type settings
tasks.outputs: embedded C code, equivalence test results
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: back-to-back testing of model against generated code checks equivalence; code efficiency is measurable per target
tasks.notes: The model itself is authored in simulate (control design); this node is the step from model to firmware.

tasks.name: Embedded unit and hardware-in-the-loop testing
tasks.definition: Given firmware and a simulated or real plant and bus environment, run unit, integration and hardware-in-the-loop tests and report coverage.
tasks.inputs: firmware, test cases, plant or bus simulation
tasks.outputs: test results, structural coverage, bus traces
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: coverage on reference firmware is measurable; hardware-in-the-loop setups are rig-specific

tasks.name: Embedded coding-standard and runtime-error verification
tasks.definition: Given embedded C or C++ source, check compliance with coding standards such as MISRA and prove the absence of runtime errors.
tasks.inputs: embedded source, coding standard, target configuration
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Juliet suite and SV-COMP embedded tasks give labeled defects

tasks.name: Embedded Linux image building
tasks.definition: Given a board definition and package selection, build a bootable root file system, kernel and bootloader for an embedded processor.
tasks.inputs: board support layers, package recipes, configuration
tasks.outputs: bootable image, software bill of materials
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: build time and bit-for-bit reproducibility are measurable

capabilities.name: Application frameworks and servers
capabilities.definition: Given application logic, provide the frameworks, runtimes and servers that turn it into a web, mobile or desktop application serving users.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software notations and tools > Development frameworks and environments > Application specific development environments
Information systems > World Wide Web > Web applications

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Web and mobile application platforms and frameworks'. Broadened to include desktop GUI, low-code builders, browsers and application and transaction servers, because O*NET assigns these categories here and they are the same layer. Content management (Drupal, Joomla), game engines and UI mockup tools are handed to media.

tasks.name: Server-side web frameworks
tasks.definition: Given routes, data models and business logic, handle HTTP requests and render responses or API payloads.
tasks.inputs: application code, routes, templates, data models

crosswalk.label: Information systems > World Wide Web > Web applications

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks measure throughput on fixed request types; app-generation benchmarks score functional correctness

tasks.name: Browser user-interface frameworks
tasks.definition: Given component definitions and application state, render and update an interactive user interface in the browser.
tasks.inputs: components, state, events
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: js-framework-benchmark measures render and update cost on fixed operations

tasks.name: Web browser engines
tasks.definition: Given HTML, CSS and JavaScript from the web, fetch, lay out, render and execute the page securely.
tasks.inputs: web resources (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media)
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Web Platform Tests score standards conformance; Speedometer and JetStream score speed

tasks.name: Mobile application frameworks
tasks.definition: Given app logic and screens, build a native or cross-platform app for phone and tablet operating systems.
tasks.inputs: app code, UI definitions, device capabilities
onet_products: Microsoft Visual Basic.NET Compact Framework CF
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: startup time, frame rate and size are measurable on fixed apps

tasks.name: Desktop graphical interface construction
tasks.definition: Given a layout and event handlers, build a native desktop user interface, by hand or in a visual builder.
tasks.inputs: layout definitions, event handlers
onet_products: Graphical user interface GUI builder software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: screenshot-to-code benchmarks (Design2Code) score generated interfaces; builder usability is not scorable

tasks.name: Low-code application building
tasks.definition: Given forms, tables and workflow rules defined visually, generate a working data-entry application without conventional programming.
tasks.inputs: data model, forms, rules
open_tools: Oracle APEX (free to use, not open)
tasks.benchmarkable: no: output quality depends on the application specified, with no shared reference tasks

tasks.name: Web service and remote call interfaces
tasks.definition: Given service operations, expose and call them across processes or machines through REST, GraphQL, RPC or distributed-object protocols.
tasks.inputs: service contract, endpoints
onet_products: Object Management Group Object Request Broker
Distributed component object model DCOM software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: latency and throughput suites exist per protocol; interface design quality is not scorable

tasks.name: HTTP serving and reverse proxying
tasks.definition: Given web content and upstream services, accept HTTP connections, serve static content, terminate TLS and proxy requests.
tasks.inputs: site content, virtual host and proxy configuration
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: h2spec checks protocol conformance; wrk-style load tests measure throughput and tail latency

tasks.name: Application and transaction servers
tasks.definition: Given deployed application components, host them with managed transactions, connection pools, security and clustering.
tasks.inputs: deployable application archives, resource configuration
onet_products: Oracle Java 2 Platform Enterprise Edition J2EE
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: SPECjEnterprise and transaction-throughput tests compare servers on a fixed application

capabilities.name: Database management and query
capabilities.definition: Given data and queries in a declared model (relational, document, graph, text, vector), store the data durably and answer the queries correctly and fast.

crosswalk.label: Information systems > Data management systems > Database management system engines
Information systems > Data management systems > Query languages
Data base user interface and query software

onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software
Object oriented data base management software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Database management systems and query'. Split by DB-Engines data model, with transactional and analytical relational processing separated because TPC-C and TPC-H/DS measure different engines. Added query authoring (text-to-SQL) and end-user desktop databases (Access, FileMaker), which O*NET counts heavily. Data modeling moved to data integration alongside metadata, as O*NET groups them.

tasks.name: Transactional relational processing
tasks.definition: Given a relational schema and concurrent SQL transactions, execute them with ACID guarantees and recover after failure.
tasks.inputs: schema, SQL transactions, isolation level
tasks.outputs: committed state, query results, recovery logs
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TPC-C measures transaction throughput; sqllogictest and Jepsen check correctness and isolation
tasks.notes: Hierarchical and network-model systems (IBM IMS, CA-IDMS, AS/400 Database) and object databases sit here as older transactional engines.

tasks.name: Analytical query processing
tasks.definition: Given large fact and dimension tables and analytical SQL, execute scans, joins and aggregations over columnar or massively parallel storage.
tasks.inputs: warehouse tables, analytical SQL

crosswalk.label: Information systems > Data management systems > Database management system engines > Online analytical processing engines

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TPC-H, TPC-DS, ClickBench and the Join Order Benchmark give fixed queries and data at known scales

tasks.name: Key-value, document and wide-column storage
tasks.definition: Given records addressed by key or document, store and retrieve them at scale with partitioning, replication and tunable consistency.
tasks.inputs: records or documents, access patterns, consistency settings
tasks.outputs: reads and writes with latency and consistency guarantees
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: YCSB defines standard workloads; Jepsen tests consistency claims

tasks.name: Graph database query
tasks.definition: Given a property graph or RDF data, answer pattern-matching and traversal queries.
tasks.inputs: nodes, edges, properties; Cypher, GQL or SPARQL queries
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the LDBC Social Network Benchmark gives audited workloads and reference results

tasks.name: Full-text search indexing
tasks.definition: Given a document collection and text queries, build inverted indexes and return ranked matches.
tasks.inputs: documents, analyzers, queries
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: MS MARCO and BEIR score ranking quality; Rally-style suites measure indexing and query speed

tasks.name: Vector similarity search
tasks.definition: Given high-dimensional embeddings and query vectors, return approximate nearest neighbors quickly at a target recall.
tasks.inputs: embedding vectors, index parameters, query vectors
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ann-benchmarks and big-ann-benchmarks report recall against queries per second

tasks.name: Query authoring and text-to-SQL
tasks.definition: Given a database schema and a question in natural language or a visual query builder, produce a correct query and its results.
tasks.inputs: schema, question or query-builder selections

crosswalk.label: Information systems > Data management systems > Query languages

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Spider and BIRD score text-to-SQL by execution accuracy

tasks.name: Database administration and tuning
tasks.definition: Given a running database and its workload, choose indexes, configuration and query plans that meet performance targets and keep the instance healthy.
tasks.inputs: workload traces, schema, configuration
tasks.outputs: index and configuration recommendations, health alerts
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: index and knob tuners can be scored on TPC-H and Join Order Benchmark workloads, as in published tuning studies

tasks.name: Desktop and end-user databases
tasks.definition: Given a small data model defined by a non-programmer, create tables, forms, queries and reports in a single-file or hosted database.
tasks.inputs: tables, forms, simple queries
tasks.outputs: working database with forms and reports
tasks.benchmarkable: no: value depends on the user's application; there is no reference task set

capabilities.name: Data integration and pipelines
capabilities.definition: Given data spread across systems and formats, move, transform, reconcile and describe it so that downstream systems can use it.

crosswalk.label: Information systems > Data management systems > Information integration
Information systems > Data management systems > Information integration > Extraction, transformation and loading
App Definition and Development > Streaming & Messaging

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Data integration, warehousing, metadata and big-data processing'. Warehouse engines moved to databases (analytical query processing); this capability keeps the movement and transformation of data, distributed batch and stream processing, messaging and the enterprise service bus, master data, and data modeling with metadata.

tasks.name: Extract, transform and load
tasks.definition: Given source systems and target schemas, extract records, apply transformations and quality rules, and load the target incrementally.
tasks.inputs: source connections, mappings, transformation rules
tasks.outputs: loaded target tables, rejected records, run logs

crosswalk.label: Information systems > Data management systems > Information integration > Extraction, transformation and loading

onet_products: Microsoft SQL Server Integration Services SSIS
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TPC-DI defines a reference data-integration workload with validation

tasks.name: Data pipeline orchestration
tasks.definition: Given a graph of dependent jobs and their schedules, run them in order, retry failures and record lineage of each run.
tasks.inputs: job definitions, dependencies, schedules
tasks.outputs: executed runs, status, retries, run history
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: scheduler overhead and failure recovery can be measured on synthetic DAGs; no standard suite

tasks.name: Distributed batch processing
tasks.definition: Given a large dataset and a data-parallel program, partition and execute it across a cluster with fault tolerance.
tasks.inputs: distributed datasets, map-reduce or dataflow program
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TPC-DS on Spark, TeraSort and HiBench give fixed workloads with known outputs

tasks.name: Messaging and stream processing
tasks.definition: Given continuous event streams, deliver them reliably between producers and consumers and compute windowed results with bounded latency.
tasks.inputs: event streams, topics or queues, streaming queries
tasks.outputs: delivered messages, continuous results, lag metrics
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the OpenMessaging Benchmark measures broker throughput and latency; Nexmark gives streaming queries with reference semantics

tasks.name: Application integration and service bus
tasks.definition: Given applications with different interfaces, route, transform and orchestrate messages between them, including business-to-business document exchange.
tasks.inputs: application endpoints, message formats, routing rules
tasks.outputs: integrated flows, transformed messages, exchange acknowledgments
tasks.benchmarkable: no: integration value is in fitting specific systems; there are no reference integration tasks
tasks.notes: EDI is listed for its transport and translation function; trading-partner processes belong to enterprise and commerce.

tasks.name: Data format transformation and schema mapping
tasks.definition: Given data in one structured format or schema, map and convert it to another format or schema.
tasks.inputs: source documents or records, source and target schemas
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the W3C XSLT and JSON Schema test suites check conformance; schema-matching benchmarks such as Valentine score mappings

tasks.name: Change data capture and replication
tasks.definition: Given a source database, capture committed changes and apply them to replicas or downstream systems with ordering and low lag.
tasks.inputs: source database logs, target systems
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: replication lag and correctness can be measured on fixed write workloads

tasks.name: Master data management and record matching
tasks.definition: Given overlapping records about the same entities from several systems, match, merge and publish a single trusted record per entity.
tasks.inputs: records from source systems, matching rules
tasks.outputs: golden records, match clusters, survivorship decisions
onet_products: Oracle Master Data Management MDM Suite
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: entity-matching datasets (Abt-Buy, DBLP-ACM, Amazon-Google) give labeled matches

tasks.name: Data modeling and metadata management
tasks.definition: Given business entities and existing data sources, design logical and physical data models and maintain a catalog of datasets, definitions and lineage.
tasks.inputs: entity requirements, source schemas, pipeline definitions
tasks.outputs: data models, generated DDL, data dictionary, lineage graph
tasks.benchmarkable: no: model and catalog quality are judged by fit to the organization, not against reference answers

capabilities.name: Operating systems and virtualization
capabilities.definition: Given computer hardware, manage processes, memory, devices and users, and present virtual machines or desktops to the software above.

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software organization and properties > Contextual software domains > Operating systems
Software and its engineering > Software organization and properties > Contextual software domains > Virtual worlds software

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Operating systems, virtualization and containers'. Containers moved to cloud infrastructure, where the CNCF landscape puts orchestration. Shells and job-control languages moved here from programming languages because they drive the operating system. Screen readers and magnifiers are placed here as an operating-system accessibility function because O*NET files them under system software.

tasks.name: General-purpose operating systems
tasks.definition: Given hardware and many concurrent programs, schedule processes, manage memory, files and devices, and enforce isolation between users.
tasks.inputs: hardware, system configuration, workloads
tasks.outputs: running system, scheduling and I/O behavior

crosswalk.label: Software and its engineering > Software organization and properties > Contextual software domains > Operating systems

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: LMbench and the Phoronix Test Suite compare kernels; the Linux Test Project checks behavior
tasks.notes: Mobile systems (Apple iOS, Google Android, Windows Mobile) are the same function on handheld hardware; mainframe systems (IBM z/OS, OpenVMS) likewise.

tasks.name: Command shells and system scripting
tasks.definition: Given an administrative goal, express it as shell commands or scripts that the operating system executes.
tasks.inputs: goal or task description, system state
tasks.outputs: command sequence or script, resulting system state
onet_products: Microsoft Visual Basic Scripting Edition VBScript
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NL2Bash and Terminal-Bench score command generation by resulting system state
tasks.notes: Mainframe job control (JCL, TSO, ISPF) is the same function on z/OS.

tasks.name: Device drivers
tasks.definition: Given a hardware device and an operating system's driver model, implement the driver that exposes the device safely to the system.
tasks.inputs: device specification, kernel interfaces
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: SV-COMP Linux driver verification tasks give defects with known verdicts

tasks.name: Hardware virtualization and emulation

open_questions: Sixteen capabilities exceeds the 6 to 14 target. Merging further (for example the two security capabilities, or operating systems with cloud) would leave 9 to 10-task nodes that mix NIST CSF functions or CNCF layers. Keep 16, or merge?
Screen readers and magnifiers (O*NET 'Device drivers or system software') are placed in computing.operating_systems.screen_access. Should assistive technology instead live in health?
PyTorch, TensorFlow and Keras are placed in computing.ml_platforms.tensor_frameworks as execution infrastructure. If science treats them as its method libraries, which domain leads?
Jupyter Notebook is listed under computing.dev_tooling.code_editing as a general programming environment; science may also claim it for numerical computing.
Microsoft Access and FileMaker Pro are claimed as end-user databases (computing.databases.desktop_databases) rather than office tools in enterprise. Confirm with the enterprise author.

Splunk Enterprise appears in both security monitoring and log analysis, and Elasticsearch in both full-text search and log analysis; that follows rule 3 but the editor may want one lead home for each.
